newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador army strips support frm Bucaram - report.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador army strips support frm Bucaram - report.

text.p: Ecuador's military has withdrawn all support from embattled President Abdala Bucaram and no longer sees him as the country's legitimate head of state, national radio said on Saturday.
"Bucaram no longer has the support of the military high command," Radio Quito said in news bulletin, citing what it said were sources close to senior military officials.

"Bucaram will no longer receive military honors corresponding to the rank of chief of state and his armed guard will be limited, as is only understandable, to the security detail a former head of state is entitled to," the radio added.

The report could not be immediately confirmed but Defense Ministry sources said the military high command was preparing to issue a communique about the political crisis that has erupted since Bucaram was voted out of office by Congress on Thursday.

Bucaram, who was removed on grounds of mental incompetence, has dismissed the congressional vote as an attempted coup. He said he plans to see out his full term of office ending in August of the year 2000.

The military, which handed over power to a civilian government in 1979, is still viewed as a powerful behind-the-scenes force in Ecuador and was widely expected to play a role in choosing Bucaram's possible successor.
